beliefs.practice: Read the DocumentDB/Mongo connection string from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) at process start and create a single long-lived PyMongo MongoClient for the whole app; do not create a new MongoClient per request.

Require TLS/SSL for the MongoDB connection (tls=true), verify server certificates (disable tlsAllowInvalidCertificates), and do not embed the connection string in source control or logs; keep it only in environment or secure config stores.

Use connection-pool tuning options on MongoClient (e.g., maxPoolSize, minPoolSize, serverSelectionTimeoutMS) appropriate for the app concurrency and reuse the pool for async/fastapi workers to avoid connection storms.

Store credentials and keys in a secrets manager (Key Vault) or environment variables; never commit DOCUMENTDB_URI or OPENAI_API_KEY to repository; provide only a .env.example with placeholders in the repo.
Use least privilege database users/roles for the app (create a Mongo user restricted to the sample_banking_01 database and only the operations needed), rather than a cluster admin/root credential.

Index all fields used to join or traverse graphs (e.g., sender_account_id, receiver_account_id, transaction_id, timestamp) and create compound indexes for common filter + sort patterns (e.g., {account_id:1, timestamp:-1}).
When using $graphLookup, limit depth and use restrictSearchWithMatch to bound the search early; ensure the fields used by $graphLookup are indexed to avoid collection scans.
Put $match stages as early as possible in aggregation pipelines to reduce working set and improve pipeline performance; use allowDiskUse=True for large aggregations.

Use explain() on representative aggregation pipelines and $graphLookup queries and inspect index usage and stage-by-stage document counts to validate index effectiveness and detect unexpected COLLSCANs.
Implement transient-fault handling: treat 429 (throughput exceeded) and network errors as transient, retry with exponential backoff, and honor Retry-After when present to avoid throttling loops.

Avoid long-running synchronous analysis in request/response handlers (FastAPI endpoints); run heavy aggregation/graph jobs as background tasks or batch jobs and return job ids so UI/API remains responsive.

Do not rely on multi-document transactions for correctness-critical flows unless you have validated that the Mongo-compatible API and cluster version fully support them; prefer idempotent writes and application-level compensation where possible.

Design data model to support graph queries used by AML detection: keep transaction references (counterparty ids / transaction refs) in fields optimized for $graphLookup, and include precomputed denormalized fields if queries are frequent.
Limit the size of returned documents via projection (only requested fields) in aggregations and queries to reduce network and memory overhead when building narratives.
When seeding or bulk-loading documents, use bulk_write/bulk inserts with appropriate batch sizes and unordered mode for speed, and create indexes after bulk load when possible to speed ingestion.
Avoid excessive or redundant indexes; each index increases write latency and RU consumption—monitor index usage and drop indexes with low usage.

For vector-enabled collections, create appropriate vector indexes (e.g., HNSW/IVF/DiskANN) on embedding fields with suitable parameters (efConstruction, M, metric) matched to query latency/recall needs; verify supported index options for the DocumentDB variant before applying them.

Scrub or pseudonymize PII before sending to external LLM/embedding services (or require an explicit opt-in); if using OPENAI_API_KEY, do not send raw account IDs or transaction details unless policy permits.
Enable and collect database diagnostics: RU consumption, latency percentiles, index metrics, and slow queries; integrate with app logging/metrics and set alerts for elevated RU or 429 rates.

Mask or redact sensitive fields in application logs and structured narratives (e.g., partial account numbers) and store only the minimum data needed for investigation; enforce role-based access for exported narratives.
Add a schemaVersion field to accounts/transactions documents so analysis code and migration scripts can evolve without misinterpreting older documents.

Use database-side explain and server index statistics (indexStats, collStats) and the DocumentDB MCP/explorer to validate any index creation commands; if an index creation via the MCP tool fails, create indexes via PyMongo with background:true to avoid blocking.

Be conservative with projection of entire subdocuments during $graphLookup results: paginate or limit returned chain lengths and materialize only the attributes required to build the suspicious-activity narrative.
Implement client-side rate limiting and batching when the agent performs many lookups/embeddings to avoid burst traffic that causes throttling or spikes in RU consumption.
